subject: Integration alignment: SDK streaming + function-calls feasibility and milestones
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Stone <amelia.stone@voltera.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Integration alignment: SDK streaming + function-calls feasibility and milestones

Hi Amelia / Ravi —

Great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared record:

Summary of needs you flagged
- Low-latency customer-facing generation for live chat (target p95 < 400ms for short responses).
- Hybrid pipeline: embeddings for retrieval -> reranking -> streamed generation with function calls to your fulfillment service.
- Auditability: request/response logging and optional KV cache TTLs to comply with retention.

Key technical constraints you mentioned
- On-prem data fetchers behind a VPN (no direct outbound traffic from those services).
- Critical path can tolerate slight reranking latency if streaming generation starts earlier with a prefix.
- Must support structured JSON outputs for downstream processing (orders/events).

Proposed integration approach (high level)
1) SDK + streaming: Redwood SDK streaming enabled so client sees tokens as generated; pair with early function-call triggers when structured payloads become clear.
2) Embeddings + rerank: offline embeddings service fed into a nearest-neighbor store; reranker model runs on top in the same request path (we suggest async rerank fallback if p95 is at risk).
3) Network pattern: use a sidecar in your VPC to pull model responses and forward to on-prem fetchers (avoids inbound holes).

Deliverables we offered
- Integration checklist (attached)
- Minimal function-call schema draft for your fulfillment APIs (attached)
- Proposal for a two-week proof-of-concept: small pilot with 1 customer flow, streaming enabled + function-call end-to-end.

Asks from your side
- Confirmation of primary fulfillment endpoints and whether they accept POST /events with JSON schema.
- List of data retention window constraints (30/90/365 days).
- A technical contact for the VPN/sidecar setup (Ravi?, cc'd).

Next steps
- Karthik will follow up with a short tech note and an example SDK snippet by EOD tomorrow.
- I’ll drop the integration checklist and calendar invite for a kickoff (proposed Monday).

Thanks again — excited to get this into a short pilot phase.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: voltera-integration-checklist.xlsx, functioncall-proposal.pdf, call-recording-20260903.mp3

From: Amelia Stone <amelia.stone@voltera.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi@voltera.io>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 17:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration alignment: SDK streaming + function-calls feasibility and milestones

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear recap. This captures the discussion well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Fulfillment endpoints: yes, we expose POST /v1/fulfill that accepts JSON; payload max size is 32KB.
- Retention: legal team requires 90 days for logs; audit events must be exportable on request.
- VPN setup: Ravi is the lead; I’ve copied him to coordinate the technical handshake.

We like the pilot scope. Two quick asks: can the SDK emit a short correlation id per request so we can tie logs back to our EHR (we currently do trace_id -> patient_session mapping)? Also, any initial perf numbers you can share for a streaming + rerank path (p50/p95) would help our infra sizing.

Appreciate it — Amelia
Amelia Stone
Head of Product
Voltera

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Stone <amelia.stone@voltera.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Ravi Menon <ravi@voltera.io>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration alignment: SDK streaming + function-calls feasibility and milestones

Amelia / team —

Quick technical follow-up and a couple of concrete artifacts attached: I added a one-page perf note and a sample function-call schema inside functioncall-proposal.pdf. Highlights below:

Perf expectations (baseline, subject to model choice and sequence length)
- Streaming-only (no rerank): p50 ~ 120–180ms, p95 ~ 280–350ms (short answers, 32–64 tokens).
- Streaming with synchronous rerank (same request): p50 ~ 200–260ms, p95 ~ 450–650ms — risk of crossing your 400ms p95 target for some flows.
- Hybrid approach: start streaming earlier with an incremental prefix result; run rerank in parallel and patch final output via function call if needed. This usually keeps p95 < 420ms in our trials.

SDK specifics we propose
- correlation_id: SDK will accept an optional correlation_id header and propagate it into logs and the token stream metadata.
- function_calls: JSON-RPC style envelope for determinism; sample schema in attachment.
- streaming hooks: on_partial_response and on_final_response callbacks, with the latter including function-call trigger metadata.

Implementation tasks (candidate sprint plan)
- Week 0: Kickoff + network/sidecar proof-of-concept (env access/ports).
- Week 1: SDK integration + local validation (sidecar + sample fulfillment endpoint).
- Week 2: Pilot run with 100 sessions, perf run and logs extraction, iterate.

Open technical questions
- Are you able to run a lightweight sidecar (Linux, outbound-only) in your VPC? If not, we can propose a reverse-proxy handshake pattern.
- Any constraints on accepting function-call patches that modify previously streamed content (we can version outputs to make reconciliation deterministic).

I’ll be happy to run a 30-min tech session with your infra team this week.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment references: functioncall-proposal.pdf (schema), voltera-integration-checklist.xlsx (for kickoff items)
